The current codebase was originally designed as a simple 2D browser game. As the project grows, introducing new gameplay systems, visual effects, and eventually a 2.5D or 3D presentation becomes increasingly difficult due to tight coupling between simulation, rendering, input handling, and UI logic.

This issue proposes a major refactor aimed at modernizing the architecture, improving maintainability, and creating a solid foundation for future visual upgrades.

Goals
Separate game simulation from rendering.

Improve code organization and maintainability.

Make gameplay systems renderer-agnostic.

Enable future migration to:

Enhanced 2D visuals
2.5D rendering
Full 3D rendering (Three.js/Babylon.js)
Reduce complexity of game.js.

Improve testability and extensibility.

game.js

 ├─ Input

 ├─ Enemy AI

 └─ Progression systems

Phase 1: Core Cleanup

Split game.js into logical modules.

Introduce a central game state.

Create clear update/render separation.

Remove rendering dependencies from gameplay logic.

Standardize entity definitions.

{
  id,
  type,
  position: { x, y, z },
  velocity,
  health,
  state,
  components
}
Tasks:


Add support for optional z coordinate.

Create reusable entity utilities.

Centralize entity lifecycle management.

Create a dedicated renderer abstraction.

Example:

renderer.render(gameState);

Move all canvas drawing code into renderer modules.

Add camera abstraction.

Support depth sorting.

Support future sprite billboards.

Support world-to-screen projection.

Prepare the game for pseudo-3D rendering.

Implement shadow rendering.

Babylon.js

World state remains renderer-independent.
